Use Case: Compare current period sales to same period last year as a percentage
Full Formula: YoY % = VAR CurSales = [Total Sales] VAR PYSales = CALCULATE([Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date])) RETURN DIVIDE(CurSales - PYSales, PYSales)
How It Works: VAR caches both period totals once; SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR shifts the date filter back a year inside CALCULATE; DIVIDE guards against a zero prior-year denominator

Use Case: Show a cumulative sum up to the current date in a time series visual
Full Formula: Running Total = CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[SalesAmount]), FILTER(ALL('Date'[Date]), 'Date'[Date] <= MAX('Date'[Date])))
How It Works: ALL clears the existing date filter; FILTER rebuilds it to include every date up to and including the current row's MAX date; CALCULATE evaluates SUM under that expanded filter

Use Case: Show each product's share of its own category's total, ignoring other filters like region
Full Formula: % of Category = DIVIDE(SUM(Sales[SalesAmount]), CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[SalesAmount]), ALLEXCEPT(Products, Products[Category])))
How It Works: ALLEXCEPT clears all filters on Products except Category, so the denominator recalculates at the category level while the numerator stays at the current (e.g. product) grain

Use Case: Rank each product's sales only against other products in the same category, not the whole table
Full Formula: Rank in Category = RANKX(ALLEXCEPT(Products, Products[Category]), [Total Sales])
How It Works: ALLEXCEPT builds the comparison set as all products sharing the current row's category; RANKX then ranks the current product's [Total Sales] against that set

Use Case: Show top 5 customers by sales and group the rest into a single 'Others' row
Full Formula: Customer Group = IF(RANKX(ALL(Customers[Name]), CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[SalesAmount]))) <= 5, VALUES(Customers[Name]), "Others")
How It Works: RANKX ranks every customer against the full unfiltered list; IF checks if current customer's rank is within top 5 and either shows their name or buckets them as Others (used as a grouping column in a matrix)

Use Case: Sum only the top N products currently selected/visible via a What-If parameter
Full Formula: Top N Sales = CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[SalesAmount]), TOPN([TopN Parameter Value], ALL(Products), CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[SalesAmount]))))
How It Works: TOPN builds a dynamic table of the highest-selling N products (N pulled from a What-If parameter measure); the outer CALCULATE restricts SUM to only rows belonging to that table

Use Case: Smooth a monthly trend line using a trailing 3-month average
Full Formula: Rolling 3M Avg = AVERAGEX(DATESINPERIOD('Date'[Date], MAX('Date'[Date]), -3, MONTH), CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[SalesAmount])))
How It Works: DATESINPERIOD returns the trailing 3 months of dates ending at the current context's last date; AVERAGEX iterates those dates, recalculating monthly sales for each via CALCULATE, then averages them

Use Case: Show prior-year sales, or blank/0 gracefully when no prior-year data exists (new products, new stores)
Full Formula: PY Sales Safe = IFERROR(CALCULATE([Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date])), BLANK())
How It Works: CALCULATE + SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR shifts context back a year; IFERROR catches any evaluation error (e.g. from an incomplete date table) and substitutes BLANK() instead of showing an error in the visual

Use Case: Classify customers into Gold/Silver/Bronze tiers based on total spend thresholds
Full Formula: Customer Tier = SWITCH(TRUE(), [Total Sales] >= 10000, "Gold", [Total Sales] >= 5000, "Silver", [Total Sales] > 0, "Bronze", "No Purchases")
How It Works: SWITCH(TRUE(), ...) pattern evaluates each boolean condition top-to-bottom and returns the first match — a cleaner alternative to nested IFs for multi-tier bucketing

Use Case: Split sales between first-time and repeat customers in the same visual
Full Formula: New Customer Sales = VAR FirstPurchase = CALCULATE(MIN(Sales[OrderDate]), ALLEXCEPT(Sales, Sales[CustomerID])) RETURN CALCULATE([Total Sales], Sales[OrderDate] = FirstPurchase)
How It Works: ALLEXCEPT isolates each customer's full order history to find their true first purchase date regardless of current date filters; the outer CALCULATE then restricts sales to only that first-purchase date

Use Case: Let a slicer swap which measure a chart displays (Sales vs Profit vs Quantity)
Full Formula: Selected Metric = SWITCH(SELECTEDVALUE('Metric Selector'[Metric]), "Sales", [Total Sales], "Profit", [Total Profit], "Quantity", [Total Qty], [Total Sales])
How It Works: SELECTEDVALUE reads the single value chosen in a disconnected slicer table; SWITCH routes to the matching pre-built measure, with a default fallback as the last argument

Use Case: Calculate margin % while avoiding divide-by-zero errors when revenue is 0
Full Formula: Margin % = VAR Rev = [Total Revenue] VAR Cost = [Total Cost] RETURN DIVIDE(Rev - Cost, Rev, 0)
How It Works: VARs avoid recalculating Revenue/Cost twice; DIVIDE's third argument returns 0 instead of an error/blank when Rev is 0, keeping visuals clean

Use Case: Find the median number of items per order across all orders
Full Formula: Median Basket Size = MEDIANX(SUMMARIZE(Sales, Sales[OrderID], "OrderQty", SUM(Sales[Qty])), [OrderQty])
How It Works: SUMMARIZE first collapses line-items into one row per order with total quantity; MEDIANX then iterates that grouped table to find the median order size

Use Case: Sum sales only for high-value, non-returned orders in a specific region
Full Formula: Qualified Sales = CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[SalesAmount]), FILTER(Sales, Sales[SalesAmount] > 500 && Sales[Returned] = FALSE && Sales[Region] = "West"))
How It Works: FILTER iterates row-by-row testing all three conditions combined with && (AND); CALCULATE applies the resulting row set as the new filter context for SUM

Pattern Name: Concatenated List per Group (Dynamic Tooltip Text)

Full Formula: Products Purchased = CONCATENATEX(VALUES(Products[Name]), Products[Name], ", ", Products[Name], ASC)
How It Works: VALUES returns distinct products visible in current filter context (e.g. for one customer); CONCATENATEX joins them into a single sorted, comma-delimited string for a tooltip or card visual

Use Case: Calculate an average price weighted by quantity sold, not a simple column average
Full Formula: Weighted Avg Price = DIVIDE(SUMX(Sales, Sales[Qty]*Sales[UnitPrice]), SUMX(Sales, Sales[Qty]))
How It Works: Numerator SUMX computes total revenue row-by-row; denominator SUMX computes total quantity; DIVIDE combines them so high-volume line items influence the average more than low-volume ones
